headline: Would have canceled a Commerce Department rule that paused certain duties on solar panels from four Southeast Asian countries.
what_it_does: This resolution would have overturned a Commerce Department rule published on September 16, 2022. That rule allows a pause on certain import duties for solar cells and panels finished in Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, or Vietnam using Chinese-made parts. The pause applies only to products not already covered by an existing antidumping or countervailing duty order. The House voted on May 24, 2023, but did not override the President's veto, so the rule stayed in place.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that import solar panels and cells from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, or Vietnam
who_it_affects.how: They could have faced duties that the rule currently pauses on panels made with Chinese parts.
They would have competed with imports that could be subject to duties instead of a pause.

who_it_affects.group: Solar installers and buyers of solar panels in the US
who_it_affects.how: The cost and supply of imported panels could have been affected if the duty pause ended.
